paras: The killing of Edward Moore took place on August 24, 1900, at Brown's tank on the Norfolk and Western Railway in southwestern Virginia, when George Fitzwater, a deputy United States marshal and Baldwin Detective Agency man, shot Moore, a Black bridge hand, through the head while arresting him. A coroner's jury found the shooting accidental and Fitzwater was released. Accounts differed on why Moore was arrested at all, and the Richmond Planet answered the official account with the words "One Negro less!"

Moore, also called Ed. or Eddie Moore, was a bridge hand employed by the Norfolk and Western and was said to be from North Carolina. Fitzwater was described as a deputy U.S. marshal and a member of the Baldwin Detective Agency of Roanoke.

According to the Radford Advance, on Friday evening Fitzwater had six white men under arrest on a freight train for stealing a ride when he was told that two Black men were riding at the front end. The two men jumped from the train, and the officer followed and arrested them, resting his left hand on one man's shoulder and his right hand, holding a cocked pistol, on Moore's. He had ordered them back onto the train when a foreman doing construction work nearby told him the men were his and that he was taking them to get material.

In the Advance's telling, the officer stepped back to hear the foreman, his foot slipped, and the pistol fired. The ball entered Moore's temple and came out of his forehead, and he died almost at once.

Fitzwater gave himself up, at Christiansburg according to the Advance. A coroner's jury, which the Advance said heard eight witnesses, pronounced the shooting accidental, and he was released. No report of any further charge or proceeding against him appears in the coverage.

The first report, a Roanoke dispatch to the Richmond Times on August 26, ran as a brief paragraph beneath a story on safe-crackers at the Standard Oil office and described the shooting as accidental. A Washington Post special, reprinted in the Washington Weekly Post under the headline "Negro Shot Dead by Accident," also accepted the jury's finding but noted that Moore, "believed to be stealing a ride," was in fact on the train "by orders."

The fullest account came from the Radford Advance, which the Times reprinted on September 4 in its "Virginia Stories" column under the headings "Dropped Pistol; Killed Negro." That account called the two men "darkies," called the shooting a "terrible accident," and closed by noting that Fitzwater's friends were sorry and that he had never before had "an accident of this kind."

The Richmond Planet reprinted the same Advance text on its front page on September 8 and added a short comment of its own. "Comment is unnecessary," the Planet wrote, then asked what difference it made "in this section whether he was murdered intentionally or killed by accident."

The Times dispatch said Moore and a companion were "charged with trespass," while the Post said they were on the train by orders and the Advance reported a foreman's claim that the men worked for him. Both specials carried Roanoke datelines, but the Advance placed Brown's tank near Christiansburg.

reader.title: Killing of Edward Moore
bases: A detective serving as a deputy U.S. marshal shot a Black railroad worker while arresting him on a freight train; no crowd or mob took part (A1, A2, A3).
Two separate Roanoke specials (A1, A2) and the Radford Advance account (A3, A4) agree that Fitzwater shot and killed Moore at Brown's tank and was cleared by a coroner's jury.

accounts.label: Roanoke dispatch to the Richmond Times
accounts.gist: Fitzwater 'accidentally' killed Moore while arresting him and a companion charged with trespass, surrendered, and was exonerated by a coroner's jury.

accounts.label: Roanoke special to the Washington Post
accounts.gist: Moore was believed to be stealing a ride but was in fact on the train by orders with a companion; the coroner's jury pronounced the shooting accidental.

accounts.label: Radford Advance (officer-friendly local account)
accounts.gist: Fitzwater held six white men for stealing a ride, then arrested two Black men with a cocked pistol on Moore's shoulder; when a foreman claimed the men, the officer stepped back, slipped, and the pistol fired.

accounts.label: Richmond Planet comment
accounts.gist: The Planet said comment was unnecessary and asked what difference it made in that section whether Moore was murdered or killed by accident.

framing.detail: The Times placed the killing as a short paragraph under 'Safe Crackers in Roanoke' and called it accidental.
The Post headlined 'Negro Shot Dead by Accident' but noted Moore was on the train 'by orders'.
The Advance account, reprinted in the Times as 'Dropped Pistol; Killed Negro', called the Black men 'darkies' and stressed the officer's friends' sorrow and his clean record.
The Planet reprinted the Advance text and answered it with 'One Negro less!'

conflicts.note: The trespass charge comes from the officer's side; the Post and the foreman's statement in the Advance both indicate Moore was on the train for his work.
